data.title: Opposition Voices Suppressed by Mass Reporting
data.summary:
Accounts contradicting the campaign narrative — including customers, staff and
independent commentators — were removed or restricted following coordinated false
reporting.
data.description:
Suppressing contradiction is cheaper than out-arguing it, and platform enforcement
provides the mechanism. Where the people correcting the record are silenced, the campaign
narrative stands unopposed without the operation having to win any argument.

The effect compounds: others observe the removals and decline to speak, so the
suppression extends well beyond the accounts actually actioned. That chilling effect is
part of the impact and is worth stating even though it cannot be counted precisely.

Those suppressed are often not connected to the organisation at all, which complicates
the response — the client has no standing to appeal on their behalf, but the silence
serves the campaign against it.
data.recommendation:
* Document suppressed accounts and the timing of enforcement; the pattern is what platforms
  act on.
* Raise the pattern with platform integrity teams rather than appealing individual
  decisions the client has no standing in.
* Record the chilling effect as an impact even where it cannot be quantified.
data.short_recommendation: Document the enforcement pattern and raise it with platform integrity teams.
